title: Amortization schedule drifts a few cents from the bank on long loans
measures: Correct math: exact rational interest per month rounded half-to-even, level payment = exact annuity formula rounded up (ceiling of an exact value, 0% = ceil(B/n)), schedule stops on the first month where balance + interest fits in one payment, and a rate change re-amortizes over months - m + 1. The tempting fix rounds the float interest per month with a float half-even and puts the residual on the last row, which matches the issue example but fails hidden tests on near-tie interest, exact-integer annuity payments that float ceil bumps by a cent, 0% loans, early payoff, and step-rate re-amortization.
prompt: Reconciliation flagged us again. For a 250,000.00 loan at 6.5% over 360 months the bank statement says total interest 318,853.84 and a final payment of 1,569.22. We print 318,853.81 and 1,569.18. We see the same few-cent drift on most long loans. The rules we have to follow are in the README and docs/rounding.md (copied from the bank product sheet). Please make our schedules match the bank to the cent.

commits.message: feat: amortization schedules with step rates
